A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same V-CECE study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite pagination and formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original counterfactual-generation experiments on BDD100K and Visual Genome, classifier analyses, and a 31-participant human evaluation, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original generation experiments, classifier analyses and 31-participant human evaluation reported in Tables 1–5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The semantic matching, three edit-ordering strategies, grounding/segmentation and frozen diffusion pipeline are unchanged. The generation settings added to Section 3.3 already appeared in v1 Appendix C; explicitly identifying WordNet clarifies the existing implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate BDD100K driving decisions and VG-Random scene classification. Medical-domain evaluation and realistic-noise testing are proposed as future work in v2, without additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains STEEX, DiME, ACE's two variants and TIME; Table 4 retains Dervakos et al. and Dimitriou et al. The new explanation of STEEX/ACE masking does not change comparator membership or reported comparisons.

E3.justification: The classifiers, metrics, editing procedures and human-study design remain unchanged. The 40 diffusion steps, sampler and upscaling settings repeated in v2 Section 3.3 were already documented in v1 Appendix C. Revised memory-use reporting does not establish a changed evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: Edit-ordering comparisons, thinking-versus-no-thinking analyses, concept-importance and ambiguity analyses, qualitative cases, and appendix survey breakdowns are retained. Noise, masking and segmentation investigations in the new limitations section are future plans.

E5.justification: Both versions report seven classifications per image, majority voting, the same standard deviations and the same seed description in Appendix C. v2 discusses limited statistical power and proposes rater-reliability analysis without adding uncertainty estimates or changing reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Section 4 revises reported average GPU memory consumption from 14% (6.7 GB) to 70% (33.6 GB) on the same 48 GB L40S. Benchmark and human-survey values in Tables 1–5, empirical plots and appendix findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The edit-cost definitions, Equations 1–2, bipartite-matching argument and optimality discussion are retained. Correcting the target concept's subscript in Section 3.1 is a notation correction without altered mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of optimal conceptual edits, training-free black-box operation and differing human alignment across classifier families. The added closing aspiration does not establish a new scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the assertion that explaining DenseNet through human semantics is 'pointless' with a qualification tied to the studied dataset and metrics. New Section 5 acknowledges the human cohort's limited size and scope, restricted statistical power/generalizability, and unresolved rater-reliability and robustness questions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project/code access link and an inpainting model identifier, explicitly identifies WordNet, and revises GPU memory-use reporting. Appendix prompts and hyperparameters remain unchanged; their partial repetition in the main text supplies no new settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Filandrianos et al.'s Conceptual Edits as Counterfactual Explanations and Rombach et al.'s latent-diffusion work. It also clarifies how V-CECE's use of masks differs from STEEX and ACE. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 adds Limitations and Future Work and Acknowledgment sections, expands selected explanations, and repeats generation details from Appendix C in Section 3.3. Most prose, the main narrative sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with more explicit component labels and an expanded caption. Main tables receive revised rules/alignment, captions are restyled, and Table 5 moves to the following page. The empirical figures and their plotted content are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 more clearly acknowledges weaknesses in the human evaluation and qualifies an overgeneralized DenseNet interpretation. The code-access information and revised pipeline diagram also improve usability. These are limited reporting gains: empirical and theoretical support is unchanged, and broad conclusion wording and the inconsistency between DenseNet's stated incorrect-image rate and Table 2's correct-image rate remain.
